channel.title: Scout Daily — AI Intelligence Feed
channel.description: Daily AI case studies and industry news for IT engineers and AI consultants.

item.title: Draft Calibration for Speculative Decoding: Accelerating LLM Serving by Matching Draft and Target Distributions
item.description:
Speculative decoding speeds up LLM inference by letting a lightweight draft model propose tokens, but it stalls when the draft’s probability distribution mismatches the main model. The authors calibrated the draft with simple temperature scaling, boosting token acceptance by about 10% and improving throughput. This directly benefits any infra team running LLM services.

IT Breakdown: If you manage LLM inference, 1) apply a temperature scaling step to your draft model before serving; 2) monitor acceptance rates and adjust the temperature until you hit a ~10% lift; 3) measure throughput to confirm the expected speed‑up.

item.title: Shifter Quantization: Compact Representations for Native Integer Computation
item.description:
Shifter Quantization (SQ) and its SHI variant let you run low‑bit integer matrix‑multiply (up to INT4) for LLMs with less accuracy loss and faster inference, especially during prefill. They reconstruct full‑width operands by appending shared bits, yielding up to 3.8× faster 2‑bit prefill and 27% faster 8‑bit batch throughput while cutting KL divergence significantly. This can improve your GPU utilisation and reduce compute costs for large‑scale LLM inference.

IT Breakdown: If you manage GPU inference for LLMs, 1) benchmark your current quantisation against SQ/SHI for your model size, 2) switch to SQ‑based INT4 kernels for 4‑bit workloads, 3) use SQ2 for 2‑bit when you need very fast prefill throughput.

item.title: [News] OpenAI says heavy ChatGPT users may hit limits sooner as it merges Chat and Work
item.description: OpenAI is merging its ChatGPT and Work experiences, introducing a shared usage meter that may cause heavy users to hit limits sooner. The change is rolling out now to a select group of Pro subscribers, with broader deployment planned for December.

item.title: [News] MCP servers can now deliver AI agent skills, changing what companies approve when they connect one
item.description: Anthropic has introduced Skills support over the Model Context Protocol (MCP) for Claude and Claude Code, now in public beta. This allows AI agents to access external services via MCP, expanding the capabilities of Claude models.

item.title: [News] The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features
item.description: Adobe’s November 2027 Photoshop update introduces AI features that automatically embed C2PA metadata marking images as AI‑edited, prompting The New York Times to forbid photographers from using the new version to preserve editorial trust.

item.title: [News] Jensen Huang broke Nvidia’s code of conduct, and his employees may not forget it
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to violating the company’s code of conduct during a recent all‑hands meeting, sparking discussion on executive accountability and corporate culture. The incident highlights how leadership actions can affect employee morale and trust, even though it has no direct impact on IT tools or infrastructure.

item.title: [News] S&P considers Nvidia credit downgrade over governance and ‘key man’ risks
item.description: S&P Global Ratings is evaluating a downgrade of Nvidia’s credit rating due to governance concerns and key‑man risk tied to CEO Jensen Huang. The downgrade could increase Nvidia’s borrowing costs, indirectly affecting customers and partners that rely on Nvidia for AI infrastructure financing.
